fieldExistenceAudit.onThisSubject: G27 v1's top-level keys were enumerated: it has no namedCorpusNotAuthored, no whatThisCloses, no leftoverDesignClosedIfAcceptedAndRecorded and no leftoverNameNote. The join asserts none of them — zero occurrences of each — and instead names liveHarnessCellVerbatim twice, which is the field that exists and does carry the corpus phrase. coordinatorSummary: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. Twenty-eight attacks run, none landed. Custody holds: subject 802268da at 0444, 11800 bytes, unmoved; HEAD never left 5d5d778 and recordedInputs.HEAD equals the top-level head; required-now 26 of 26; file 08 and COORD unmodified and matching their pins; all nine recordedInputs files reproduce with basedOn cross-checked at zero disagreements, including the g27-input-corpus.v1 subject at d4dd7e61 — the digest I measured when reviewing that corpus — and my verdict on it. The sealed-Run prohibition holds structurally rather than by disclaimer. I probed for what a class would actually look like: zero isSealed, zero sealed: key, zero quoted sealed key, zero promoteTo, zero runClass. No schema, field set, membership predicate or comparison target exists anywhere in the file. Of the thirteen string fields touching sealed or G19, eleven are refusals or quotations of the register's own cells and the other two are the harness path and its review path, which carry not-sealed-run inside the filename. That matters because G27 v1's own EV-1 says the specification retains the absence of the label rather than inventing a class to compare against, and the join keeps to that. The second result is family-wide. Two reviews ago I filed CLAUDE-G18LJ-V2-SF1 because a join asserted a source its target did not contain, so rather than test that shape only here I measured it across every gate join I have reviewed today. G27 v1 has no whatThisCloses and therefore no leftoverDesignClosedIfAcceptedAndRecorded, and no leftoverNameNote — I enumerated its keys rather than searching for names — and the join asserts neither, naming liveHarnessCellVerbatim instead, which exists and does carry the corpus phrase. Across G16, G18, G21, G22, G23, G25 and G27 the claim appears exactly when the harness carries the field: five yes, two no, seven for seven. That is worth recording because five of the seven do assert what this one omits, so a reviewer grading by remembered shape would have called this a gap; and because it bounds my G18 finding to the axis it actually concerned, the input-corpus citation, rather than leaving it as a general suspicion of template copying. The rest holds. 'catalog' occurs zero times and the predecessor role reads named-corpus, so the G23 shape is absent. Cell [7] of the DR-G27 row is OPEN and cell [4] is byte-identical to liveGateOwners. D-153's adopted text owns DR-131 NT-6 only and closes its leftover-design with remainder at G27 execution, which the join states without reopening, and namedClassesThisGate is exactly NT-6. The input-corpus role string was measured a fifth consecutive time — three states, three distinct stateNamed values, seven exactByteIntent occurrences, all three sources citing it. The successor diff is surgical: five obligations to six, one added, none removed, doesNot byte-identical at fifteen entries, summary.leftoverDesign unchanged, and the omission of the harness-field claim is inherited from a v1 that already carries an ACCEPT. Disclosure: every Claude-lane verdict this join pins is mine. The hazard on a seventh consecutive artifact of one shape is grading from memory, and memory is precisely what would have produced a false finding here, so I replaced it with a measurement anyone can re-run.
